squirrel.services.workspace.WorkspaceService

class squirrel.services.workspace.WorkspaceService.WorkspaceService(db=None, minio=None, connector=None)[source]

Bases: object

Coordinate workspace bookkeeping and artifact persistence for the preprocessing and model-building pipelines.

Responsibilities:

  1. Create / list / fetch / rename / delete workspaces and track their lifecycle status and data type.

  2. Manage input sources per workspace: uploaded files of any supported type (stored in MinIO), or references to an existing data connector.

  3. Upload processed DataFrames and fitted models to MinIO.

  4. Insert a workspace-run row in PostgreSQL recording the S3 URLs, agent summary, and LLM metadata for each pipeline run.

  5. Expose retrieval helpers so downstream routes can fetch workspace and run history.

  6. Persist the fitted preprocessing pipeline (plan + execution report, including every strategy’s data-dependent fitted parameters) as its own MinIO artifact, and replay it — together with a saved model — against new data via predict().

Parameters:

  • db (Optional[PostgresService]) – An open PostgresService instance.

  • minio (Optional[MinIOService]) – An open MinIOService instance.

  • connector (Optional[DataConnectorService]) – An open DataConnectorService instance.

load_csv(file_url)[source]

Download a single uploaded CSV source from MinIO and load it into a DataFrame. Used internally by preview_upload_source() (and previously mirrored, less correctly, by inline logic in load_source_dataframes()).

Note

Reads directly from retrieve_file’s in-memory fileByte rather than treating fileUrl as a local filesystem path. retrieve_file returns the original s3://... URL in fileUrl (its local temp download is already deleted before it returns) — passing that straight to pd.read_csv previously hit fsspec’s own (uncredentialed, non-MinIO-aware) S3 handling and surfaced as FileNotFoundError: The specified bucket does not exist, since it was never actually reading the file this method had just downloaded.

Parameters:

file_url (str) – s3://... URL of the CSV to load.

Returns:

The parsed CSV as a DataFrame.

Return type:

pd.DataFrame

Raises:

RuntimeError – if the file can’t be retrieved from MinIO.

load_source_dataframes(sources)[source]

Resolve every input source on a workspace into an in-memory DataFrame, keyed by source_id.

  • kind == "upload": dispatched by file_type to the matching loader in _upload_loaders() (only "csv" today).

  • kind == "connector": delegated to fetch_data(). This is the extension point for wiring up the Data Connectors page’s live sources (Postgres, BigQuery, warehouses, etc.) — today it raises NotImplementedError with a clear message so the route can surface a 501 rather than a silent failure.

Parameters:

sources (List[Dict[str, Any]]) – Input-source dicts, as stored on a workspace’s input_sources.

Returns:

DataFrames keyed by source_id.

Return type:

Dict[str, pd.DataFrame]

Raises:

  • RuntimeError – if any upload source can’t be downloaded.

  • NotImplementedError – if a connector source, or an upload source whose file_type has no registered loader (e.g. a future “zip”/”txt” source), has no data-fetching implementation.

save_run(workspace_id, agent_type, input_file_urls, data, summary, prompt_tokens=0, completion_tokens=0, total_tokens=0, response_time_ms=0, owner_user_id=None, plan=None, execution_report=None)[source]

Persist one pipeline run’s output artifacts + summary.

Parameters:

  • workspace_id (str) – Workspace the run belongs to.

  • agent_type (str) – "preprocessing" or "model_building".

  • input_file_urls (List[str]) – S3 URLs of every input file consumed.

  • data (Any) – For "preprocessing", the processed DataFrame. For "model_building", a dict of {model_key: fitted_estimator}. Anything else is left unpersisted (no output artifacts uploaded).

  • summary (Dict) – Agent’s structured JSON summary of the run.

  • prompt_tokens (int) – LLM prompt token count for the run.

  • completion_tokens (int) – LLM completion token count for the run.

  • total_tokens (int) – LLM total token count for the run.

  • response_time_ms (int) – Wall-clock time the run took, in ms.

  • owner_user_id (Optional[str]) – Owning user id, recorded on the run and any uploaded artifacts.

  • plan (Optional[Any]) – For agent_type == "preprocessing" only — the JSON plan string/dict returned by TabularDataProcessorAgent.plan() (or the third element of run()/run_multi()’s return tuple). Combined with execution_report and persisted as a “fitted pipeline” artifact so predict() can later replay this exact preprocessing against new data. Ignored for other agent_type values.

  • execution_report (Optional[Any]) – For agent_type == "preprocessing" only — the JSON execution report string/dict returned by TabularDataProcessorAgent.execute() (or the fourth element of run()/run_multi()’s return tuple). This is what actually carries the fitted parameters (means, bounds, encoding maps, fitted power-transform λ, one-hot dummy-column sets, …) that predict() needs. When omitted, no pipeline artifact is saved and this workspace’s data won’t be predictable on until a run supplies one.

Returns:

{"record_id", "output_file_urls"}.

Return type:

Dict

save_pipeline_artifact(workspace_id, plan, execution_report, owner_user_id=None)[source]

Persist the preprocessing plan + execution report as one JSON artifact in MinIO.

The execution report’s per-step per_column blocks are exactly the fitted state (means, bounds, encoding maps, fitted power-transform λ, one-hot dummy-column sets, group aggregation stats, …) that predict() needs to replay this pipeline on new rows instead of re-fitting from them.

Parameters:

  • workspace_id (str) – Workspace the pipeline belongs to.

  • plan (Union[str, Dict]) – JSON plan string or dict.

  • execution_report (Union[str, Dict]) – JSON execution report string or dict.

  • owner_user_id (Optional[str]) – If provided, only save the artifact if the workspace belongs to this user. Otherwise, save for any workspace with the given workspace_id.

Returns:

The artifact’s s3:// URL, or None on failure.

Return type:

Optional[str]

predict(workspace_id, new_data, model_key=None, owner_user_id=None)[source]

Inference-time counterpart to /build.

Two distinct prediction paths, depending on the resolved model:

  • Sequential models (bilstm, lstm_attention): these are

    fit purely on the target column’s own historical values (see TabularDataModelBuilderAgent._fit_time_series_model). The target history is reconstructed from the workspace’s original input sources and forecast forward by len(new_data) steps.

  • Everything else: replays the saved preprocessing pipeline on

    new_data via TabularDataProcessorAgent.apply_fitted_pipeline using training-time fitted parameters, then predicts on the transformed result.

Parameters:

  • workspace_id (str) – Workspace to predict against.

  • new_data (pd.DataFrame) – For non-sequential models: raw new rows, shaped like the original input source(s) before preprocessing. For sequential models: only its row count is used, as the number of future steps to forecast.

  • model_key (Optional[str]) – Which fitted model to use. None uses the workspace’s recorded best_model.

  • owner_user_id (Optional[str]) – If provided, only predict against a workspace belonging to this user.

Returns:

{"model_key", "predictions", ["probabilities", "classes"]}.

Return type:

Dict[str, Any]

Raises:

RuntimeError – no saved pipeline, no fitted model, no target history to seed a sequential model, or model_key can’t be resolved.
